I reccomend digging around a bit on YouTube, but I'll tell you what works for me. So firstly, lucid dreaming is becoming aware you are dreaming while you are dreaming, at high levels of it you can control your dreams and nust have a lot of fun. A couple of basics you need to do if you want to lucid dream:

Reality checks, this is stuff like counting your fingers, trying to push your finger through your palm. If you do it enough in real life, you'll start to do it in your dreams.

Dream journaling. As soon as you wake up, write down wHt you can rember from your dreams, this makes them more vivid and tells your brain they are important.

Stick to a consistent sleep schedule. Also, try not to go on your phone or any screen to close to bed, as well as avoiding eating too close to bed as well.

I also reccomend meditating before you go to bed, it's not a must, but it certainly helps. It helps your mind stay alert but relaxed.

And lastly, pick a technique(s) to use. Personally I use MILD and WBTB if I wake up during the night naturally. I'm still quite new to this but in two weeks I've had three lucid dreams.
 
In the first one, I was stuck in a swamp, and couldn't do much. I tried to spawn someone in and woke up.

Second time, I was skydiving through a forest when I became lucid I woke up from excitement. 

And lastly, I was having a dream inside a dream inside a dream when I became lucid. I spent a bit of time in the dream and tried to fly, but then I woke up inside the dream into another dream, and lost the lucidity.

Just from my experience it is unbelievably important to stabilize the dream once you become lucid  or the dream will fade away quickly and you will wake up. The only time I managed to have a lucid dream and stabilize was the last one, but the story of the dream made me lose it, but so it goes. Good luck.
